content.title: About
content.content: Beef salad is a dish made with boiled or grilled beef, fresh vegetables (tomatoes, cucumbers, onion, pepper), herbs, and a dressing based on olive oil or yogurt. It combines protein, vitamins, and healthy fats, making it a nutritious and satisfying light meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef in the salad is often sliced thin or cubed, which speeds cooling and eases mixing.
A traditional Mediterranean version includes olives, feta cheese, and oregano.
Beef salad is popular in keto and paleo diets because of its high protein and low carbohydrate content.
Adding fresh lemon juice enhances iron absorption from the beef.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support the immune system and hemoglobin formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Including B12, B6, and niacin, they play key roles in energy metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fats in the dressing
items.content: Olive oil or avocado‑yogurt supplies monounsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Fresh veggies increase dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Choosing lean cuts and moderate portions helps reduce cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Beef should be cooked thoroughly and stored at temperatures below 4 °C.

items.title: Sodium in the dressing
items.content: Overly salty sauces can raise blood pressure; use salt sparingly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, immediately after preparation. It can be eaten on its own, wrapped in a flatbread, or used as a side dish. For variety, add avocado, nuts, or legumes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. If the dressing contains yogurt, ensure it is fresh. Stir before serving to evenly distribute the dressing.
